The default UI focuses on a dense, data-forward onboarding dashboard suitable for internal teams.\n\n### Tech stack\n- Next.js 15 · React 19 · TypeScript\n- Tailwind CSS v4 with Shadcn UI components\n- Prisma ORM with a PostgreSQL datasource\n- NextAuth (database sessions) using the Prisma adapter\n- nuqs for URL state management (not yet used, ready when needed)\n\n---\n\n## Prerequisites\n- Node.js 20+\n- npm 10+\n- Docker Desktop (or a local PostgreSQL 16 instance if you prefer manual setup)\n\n---\n\n## 1. Start PostgreSQL\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ndocker compose up -d postgres\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nVerify the service is healthy:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ndocker compose ps\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 3. Prisma schema &amp; seed data\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run db:migrate -- --name init\nnpm run db:seed\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUseful extras:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run prisma:generate  # Regenerate the Prisma client\nnpm run db:studio       # Launch Prisma Studio\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe default seed creates an &#96;Acme Inc&#96; organisation and a placeholder owner (&#96;owner@example.com&#96;).\n\n---\n\n## 4. Run the app\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nVisit [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Unauthenticated users are redirected to &#96;/signin&#96; where they can use Google SSO. After signing in you land on the internal onboarding overview.\n\n---\n\n## UI components\n\nShadcn UI was initialised with the “Neutral · New York” theme. Common primitives (button, card, avatar, dropdown, separator, badge, skeleton) are available under &#96;components/ui/&#96;. To add more components:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpx shadcn@latest add &lt;component&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Application structure\n\n### Navigation &amp; layouts\n- &#96;/dashboard&#96; – Dashboard overview rendered inside &#96;app/dashboard/layout.tsx&#96;\n- &#96;/users&#96; – Organization member management\n- &#96;/settings&#96; – Placeholder workspace configuration page\n- Sidebar (&#96;AppSidebar&#96;) highlights the active route and shows the current organization name\n\n### Automatic workspace provisioning\n- First-time sign-ins that lack memberships are assigned a personal organization via &#96;ensureUserMembership&#96;\n- The user becomes the org owner (&#96;role = ADMIN&#96;) and gains immediate access to dashboard/users/settings\n\n### User management flows\n- &#96;app/dashboard/users/page.tsx&#96; lists all members in the active organization\n- &#96;UserList&#96; displays avatar, email, role badge, join date, and action menu\n- Invite users via the “Invite User” dialog:\n  1. Enter email + desired role\n  2. Existing users are added to the organization; new emails create placeholder accounts that can sign in with Google\n\n### Role-based permissions\n- Roles: &#96;ADMIN&#96;, &#96;MEMBER&#96;\n- Admin-only capabilities:\n  - Invite users\n  - Update member roles\n  - Remove members (cannot remove self or the last admin)\n- Permission helpers live in &#96;lib/permissions.ts&#96; and guard both UI and API routes\n\n### API routes\n| Route | Method | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;/api/users&#96; | &#96;GET&#96; | List all members in the current organization |\n| &#96;/api/users/[id]&#96; | &#96;PATCH&#96; | Update a member’s role (admin-only) |\n| &#96;/api/users/[id]&#96; | &#96;DELETE&#96; | Remove a member (admin-only, safeguards last admin) |\n| &#96;/api/users/invite&#96; | &#96;POST&#96; | Invite/add a user to the organization |\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\n| Layer | Details |\n| --- | --- |\n| Frontend | Next.js 15 App Router with shared root layout (&#96;app/layout.tsx&#96;) for session hydration and &#96;app/dashboard/layout.tsx&#96; for protected routes. |\n| Auth | NextAuth + Prisma adapter (Google provider). Session helpers in &#96;lib/auth.ts&#96;, client hydration via &#96;AuthProvider&#96;. |\n| RBAC | Membership + role helpers in &#96;lib/permissions.ts&#96;, organization auto-provisioning in &#96;lib/organizations.ts&#96;. |\n| Data | Prisma ORM targeting Postgres (Docker locally).   "contentsAfterEdit": "# Auth &amp; RBAC Strategy\n\n## Authentication\n- **Provider:** NextAuth with Google OAuth (Prisma adapter, database sessions).\n- **Session Hydration:** &#96;auth()&#96; helper in &#96;app/layout.tsx&#96; fetches server-side session → &#96;AuthProvider&#96; for client components.\n- **Callbacks:**\n  - &#96;jwt&#96; callback loads membership roles on initial sign-in and stores as &#96;token.organizationRoles&#96;.\n  - &#96;session&#96; callback exposes &#96;session.user.organizationRoles&#96; for layouts/components.\n\n## Roles\n- Enum &#96;MembershipRole&#96; defined in Prisma schema: &#96;ADMIN&#96;, &#96;MEMBER&#96;, &#96;SUPPLIER&#96;, &#96;PROCUREMENT&#96;, &#96;MDM&#96;.\n- Memberships tie a user to an organization with a specific role.\n- Internal dashboards currently use ADMIN/MEMBER; supplier/internal personas introduced in future phases.\n\n## Permission Helpers\n- &#96;lib/permissions.ts&#96;\n  - &#96;getCurrentUserMembership()&#96; fetches membership (used in API routes).\n  - &#96;isAdmin&#96; / &#96;requireAdmin&#96; guard sensitive routes (user management).\n  - Future utility: &#96;requireRole(role, organizationId)&#96; to support PROC/MDM flows.\n\n## Session Shape\n&#96;&#96;&#96;ts\nsession.user = {\n  id,\n  name?,\n  email?,\n  organizationRoles: Array&lt;{ organizationId: string; role: MembershipRole }&gt;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n- Accessible in layouts/components for conditional rendering (e.g., admin-only buttons).\n\n## Access Patterns\n- **Layouts:** Protected &#96;app/dashboard/layout.tsx&#96; redirects unauthenticated users to &#96;/signin&#96;.\n- **API Routes:** All &#96;/api/users/*&#96; routes call &#96;auth()&#96; + &#96;requireAdmin&#96; before mutating memberships.\n- **Auto-Provisioning:** &#96;ensureUserMembership&#96; callback.\n"

```json
  "contentsAfterEdit": "# Foundation Architecture Overview\n\n## Request Flow\n1. **Client Request** hits Next.js App Router.\n2. **Root layout (&#96;app/layout.tsx&#96;)** fetches session via &#96;auth()&#96; helper and hydrates &#96;AuthProvider&#96;.\n3. **Nested layouts** (e.g., &#96;app/dashboard/layout.tsx&#96;) enforce auth, load organization context, and render shared UI (sidebar, header).\n4. **Server Components** fetch data using Prisma (&#96;lib/prisma.ts&#96;).\n5. **API Routes (app/api/...)** handle mutations with NextAuth session guard + Prisma writes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nBrowser → Next.js App Router → Layout tree → Server components / Route handlers → Prisma → Postgres\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Auth Touchpoints\n- &#96;lib/auth.ts&#96; defines &#96;authOptions&#96;, combines PrismaAdapter + Google provider.\n- NextAuth callbacks (Phase 1) will enrich &#96;jwt&#96; + &#96;session&#96; with role/org claims (see [NextAuth docs](https://context7.com/nextauthjs/docs/llms.txt)).\n- &#96;AuthProvider&#96; (client) wraps app for client-side session hooks when needed.\n\n## Shared Utilities\n- &#96;lib/permissions.ts&#96; – role checks (&#96;isAdmin&#96;, &#96;canManageUsers&#96;).\n- &#96;lib/organizations.ts&#96; – auto-create personal workspace on first login.\n- &#96;components/providers/sidebar-provider.tsx&#96; – manages responsive sidebar state.\n- &#96;components/navigation/app-sidebar.tsx&#96; – route-aware navigation w/ org name.\n\n## Data Access &amp; Persistence\n- Prisma Client instantiated once via &#96;lib/prisma.ts&#96; (global caching for dev).\n- Migrations run via &#96;npm run db:migrate&#96;; seeds via &#96;npm run db:seed&#96;.\n- Current schema: users, accounts, sessions, organizations, memberships, documents (future), etc.\n\n## Deployment Targets (placeholder)\n- Local: Dockerized Postgres, &#96;npm run dev&#96;.\n- Staging/Prod: Vercel hosting, managed Postgres (Supabase/RDS) to be determined.\n\n## Next Steps\n- Expand schema per Phase 1.\n- Formalize ADR for staying on NextAuth + Prisma.\n"
}
```

```json
  "contentsAfterEdit": "\"use client\";\n\nimport { useTransition } from \"react\";\nimport {\n  claimApplicationAction,\n  transitionApplicationAction,\n} from \"@/app/dashboard/procurement/[id]/actions\";\nimport { nextActions } from \"@/lib/application-state\";\n\ninterface ActionPanelProps {\n  applicationId: string;\n  currentStatus: string;\n}\n\nexport function ProcurementActionPanel({\n  applicationId,\n  currentStatus,\n}: ActionPanelProps) {\n  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();\n\n  const handleTransition = (target: string) =&gt; {\n    startTransition(async () =&gt; {\n      await transitionApplicationAction({\n        applicationId,\n        targetStatus: target as\n          | \"IN_REVIEW\"\n          | \"PENDING_SUPPLIER\"\n          | \"APPROVED\"\n          | \"REJECTED\",\n      });\n    });\n  };\n\n  const handleClaim = () =&gt; {\n    startTransition(async () =&gt; {\n      await claimApplicationAction(applicationId);\n    });\n  };\n\n  return (\n    &lt;div className=\"space-y-3 rounded-2xl border border-slate-200 bg-white p-4 text-sm\"&gt;\n      &lt;p className=\"text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.3em] text-slate-500\"&gt;\n        Actions\n      &lt;/p&gt;\n      &lt;button\n        type=\"button\"\n        onClick={handleClaim}\n        disabled={isPending}\n        className=\"w-full rounded-full border border-slate-200 px-4 py-2 font-medium text-slate-900\"\n      &gt;\n        Claim application\n      &lt;/button&gt;\n      &lt;div className=\"grid gap-2 sm:grid-cols-2\"&gt;\n        {nextActions\n          .filter((action) =&gt; action.value !== currentStatus)\n          .map((action) =&gt; (\n            &lt;button\n              key={action.value}\n              type=\"button\"\n              onClick={() =&gt; handleTransition(action.value)}\n              disabled={isPending}\n              className=\"rounded-full bg-slate-900 px-4 py-2 text-white disabled:opacity-50\"\n            &gt;\n              {action.label}\n            &lt;/button&gt;\n          ))}\n      &lt;/div&gt;\n      &lt;p className=\"text-xs text-slate-500\"&gt;\n        Actions enforce the SUBMITTED → IN_REVIEW → (PENDING_SUPPLIER | APPROVED\n        | REJECTED) workflow.\n      &lt;/p&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n  );\n}\n\n"
}
```

```json
  "contentsAfterEdit": "## Supplier Hub SaaS Starter\n\nA compact internal SaaS starter that pairs **Next.js 15 (App Router)** with **React 19**, **Tailwind CSS v4**, **Shadcn UI**, **Prisma**, **NextAuth (Google SSO)**, and a Dockerised PostgreSQL database. The default UI focuses on a dense, data-forward onboarding dashboard suitable for internal teams.\n\n### Tech stack\n- Next.js 15 · React 19 · TypeScript\n- Tailwind CSS v4 with Shadcn UI components\n- Prisma ORM with a PostgreSQL datasource\n- NextAuth (database sessions) using the Prisma adapter\n- nuqs for URL state management (not yet used, ready when needed)\n\n---\n\n## Prerequisites\n- Node.js 20+\n- npm 10+\n- Docker Desktop (or a local PostgreSQL 16 instance if you prefer manual setup)\n\n---\n\n## 1. Environment variables\n\nCopy the sample env file and fill in the values:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncp env.example .env.local\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nRequired values:\n\n| Variable | Description |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;DATABASE_URL&#96; / &#96;DIRECT_URL&#96; | Connection strings for local Postgres (already set for Docker Compose) |\n| &#96;NEXTAUTH_SECRET&#96; | &#96;openssl rand -hex 32&#96; or similar |\n| &#96;NEXTAUTH_URL&#96; | Base URL (e.g. &#96;http://localhost:3000&#96;) |\n| &#96;GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID&#96; / &#96;GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET&#96; | From your Google OAuth credentials |\n| &#96;NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL&#96; | Used for absolute links in the UI |\n\n&gt; **Google OAuth redirect URI:** &#96;http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 2. Start PostgreSQL\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ndocker compose up -d postgres\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nVerify the service is healthy:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ndocker compose ps\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## 3. Prisma schema &amp; seed data\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run db:migrate -- --name init\nnpm run db:seed\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUseful extras:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run prisma:generate  # Regenerate the Prisma client\nnpm run db:studio       # Launch Prisma Studio\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe default seed creates an &#96;Acme Inc&#96; organisation and a placeholder owner (&#96;owner@example.com&#96;).\n\n---\n\n## 4. Run the app\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nVisit [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Unauthenticated users are redirected to &#96;/signin&#96; where they can use Google SSO. After signing in you land on the internal onboarding overview.\n\n---\n\n## UI components\n\nShadcn UI was initialised with the “Neutral · New York” theme. Common primitives (button, card, avatar, dropdown, separator, badge, skeleton) are available under &#96;components/ui/&#96;. To add more components:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpx shadcn@latest add &lt;component&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Application structure\n\n### Navigation &amp; layouts\n- &#96;/dashboard&#96; – Dashboard overview rendered inside &#96;app/dashboard/layout.tsx&#96;\n- &#96;/dashboard/users&#96; – Organization member management\n- &#96;/dashboard/settings&#96; – Workspace configuration page\n- Sidebar (&#96;AppSidebar&#96;) highlights the active route and shows the current organization name\n\n### Automatic workspace provisioning\n- First-time sign-ins that lack memberships are assigned a personal organization via &#96;ensureUserMembership&#96;\n- The user becomes the org owner (&#96;role = ADMIN&#96;) and gains immediate access to &#96;/dashboard/users&#96; and &#96;/dashboard/settings&#96;\n\n### User management flows\n- &#96;app/dashboard/users/page.tsx&#96; lists all members in the active organization\n- &#96;UserList&#96; displays avatar, email, role badge, join date, and action menu\n- Invite users via the “Invite User” dialog:\n  1. Enter email + desired role\n  2. Existing users are added to the organization; new emails create placeholder accounts that can sign in with Google\n\n### Role-based permissions\n- Roles: &#96;ADMIN&#96;, &#96;MEMBER&#96;\n- Admin-only capabilities:\n  - Invite users\n  - Update member roles\n  - Remove members (cannot remove self or the last admin)\n- Permission helpers live in &#96;lib/permissions.ts&#96; and guard both UI and API routes\n\n### API routes\n| Route | Method | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| &#96;/api/users&#96; | &#96;GET&#96; | List all members in the current organization |\n| &#96;/api/users/[id]&#96; | &#96;PATCH&#96; | Update a member’s role (admin-only) |\n| &#96;/api/users/[id]&#96; | &#96;DELETE&#96; | Remove a member (admin-only, safeguards last admin) |\n| &#96;/api/users/invite&#96; | &#96;POST&#96; | Invite/add a user to the organization |\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\n| Layer | Details |\n| --- | --- |\n| Frontend | Next.js 15 App Router with shared root layout (&#96;app/layout.tsx&#96;) for session hydration and &#96;app/dashboard/layout.tsx&#96; for protected routes. |\n| Auth | NextAuth + Prisma adapter (Google provider). Session helpers in &#96;lib/auth.ts&#96;, client hydration via &#96;AuthProvider&#96;. |\n| RBAC | Membership + role helpers in &#96;lib/permissions.ts&#96;, organization auto-provisioning in &#96;lib/organizations.ts&#96;. |\n| Data | Prisma ORM targeting Postgres (Docker locally). Migrations via &#96;npm run db:migrate&#96;, seeds via &#96;npm run db:seed&#96;. |\n| UI Shell | Shadcn UI components + custom sidebar provider. |\n| Docs | Detailed phase plans + foundation/security docs in &#96;/docs&#96;. |\n\nSee &#96;/docs/foundation-architecture.md&#96; and &#96;/docs/security-baseline.md&#96; for diagrams, session strategy, and environment matrix.\n\n---\n\n## Next steps &amp; recommendations\n- Replace the seed data with your production schema and add Prisma migrations as you evolve the database.\n- Extend the Shadcn component library as you build out new flows.\n- Configure additional NextAuth callbacks (e.g. RBAC) once you introduce role-specific surfaces.\n- Add integration tests under &#96;supplier_capabilities/tests&#96; per project convention.\n\n---\n\n## Available scripts\n\n| Command | Description |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;npm run dev&#96; | Start the Next.js dev server |\n| &#96;npm run build&#96; | Create a production build |\n| &#96;npm run start&#96; | Run the production server |\n| &#96;npm run lint&#96; | Execute ESLint |\n| &#96;npm run db:migrate&#96; | Apply Prisma migrations |\n| &#96;npm run db:seed&#96; | Seed the database with fixtures |\n| &#96;npm run prisma:generate&#96; | Regenerate the Prisma client |\n| &#96;npm run db:studio&#96; | Open Prisma Studio |\n"
}
```

```json
  "contentsAfterEdit": "# Phase 4 – Admin Configuration Console\n\n## Objectives\n- Empower admins to manage entities, geographies, form configs, document requirements, and integrations via UI.\n- Generate validation schemas from stored config and expose them to supplier/procurement flows.\n\n## Functional Modules\n1. **Entities &amp; Geographies**\n   - CRUD screens for legal entities (Zetwerk, Unimacts, Spectrum, etc.).\n   - Mapping table for which geographies each entity supports.\n2. **Form Builder**\n   - Manage form configs per (entity, geography, version).\n   - Section + field designers with drag/sort, metadata (labels, tooltips, validations, conditional logic).\n   - Preview panel rendering the resulting form.\n3. **Document Requirements**\n   - Define document types (tax, bank, legal) and mark required/optional per config.\n4. **Integrations &amp; Settings**\n   - Freshdesk API keys/group IDs, email templates, future ERP settings (exposed in &#96;/dashboard/settings&#96;).\n5. **Access Control**\n   - Admin-only route group (&#96;/dashboard/admin&#96;) guarded by NextAuth role check + server actions verifying &#96;ADMIN&#96; role.\n\n## Status\n- ✅ Admin route + navigation entries wired (dashboard sidebar now links to Procurement + Admin, gated via &#96;requireRole&#96;).\n- ✅ Entities &amp; geographies CRUD delivered (card UIs with server actions backing &#96;prisma.entity&#96; / &#96;prisma.geography&#96;).\n- ✅ Form builder MVP: admins can create form configs per entity+geo, add sections inline, and see latest configs.\n- ✅ Document requirement management (document type catalog + per-config flags) shipped.\n- ✅ Integrations/settings page (Freshdesk domain/API key, email templates) live under &#96;/dashboard/settings&#96;.\n- ✅ Schema generator + preview ( &#96;lib/form-schema.ts&#96; + admin preview card) and admin change history logging.\n\n## Implementation Steps\n1. Build &#96;/admin&#96; layout with navigation (Entities, Forms, Documents, Integrations, Users). ✅\n2. Implement CRUD APIs using Prisma + server actions; add optimistic UI updates. ✅ Entities/geos/form configs handled via server actions.\n3. Create shared components (FieldEditor, ValidationRuleEditor, DocumentRequirementTable). ⚙️ Sections UI in place; field/doc editors backlog.\n4. Create schema generator service:\n   - Input: form config JSON.\n   - Output: Zod schema used by supplier wizard + procurement view. ✅\n5. Add change history (audit log entries) for admin actions. ✅\n\n## Deliverables\n- Admin console UI + APIs.\n- &#96;lib/form-schema.ts&#96; generator producing Zod schema from DB config.\n- Documentation: &#96;/docs/admin-console.md&#96; describing workflows and guardrails.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- Admin can create new form version for an entity/geo and preview schema.\n- Changes persist in DB and propagate to supplier wizard (after publish toggle).\n- Integrations page securely stores encrypted secrets (if supported) or references env variables.\n\n## Risks &amp; Mitigations\n- **Complex UI:** start with table-based CRUD before drag/drop; iterate.\n- **Schema drift:** add unit tests verifying generator output vs sample config.\n- **Security:** enforce role guards on both UI and API layers; log admin actions.\n"
```

### Routing & Navigation
- Sidebar destinations now point to `/dashboard/*`, and the Admin item is labeled “Configuration” so the shell highlights the correct section after the route-group rename.  
```23:48:components/navigation/app-sidebar.tsx
const menuItems = [
  { title: "Dashboard", url: "/dashboard", icon: LayoutDashboard },
  { title: "Users", url: "/dashboard/users", icon: Users },
  { title: "Procurement", url: "/dashboard/procurement", icon: Briefcase },
  { title: "Settings", url: "/dashboard/settings", icon: Settings },
  { title: "Configuration", url: "/dashboard/admin", icon: ShieldCheck },
];
```
- Legacy bookmarks hitting `/users` or `/settings` now get redirected to the new dashboard routes, so those URLs no longer 404.

- Freshdesk domain/API key/email template management moved from the admin console to `/dashboard/settings`, where each org renders its own form backed by the same `updateIntegrationsAction` (which now revalidates both settings and admin views).

### Procurement Filters
- The procurement dashboard now awaits `searchParams` before reading query keys, satisfying Next 15’s async dynamic API requirement and fixing the runtime error.  
```1:40:app/dashboard/procurement/page.tsx
type ProcurementSearchParams = { q?: string; status?: string; entity?: string; page?: string };
export default async function ProcurementDashboard({ searchParams }: ProcurementDashboardProps) {
  const params = (await searchParams) ?? {};
  const query = params.q?.trim() ?? "";
  const statusFilter = params.status;
  const entityFilter = params.entity;
  const page = Number(params.page ?? "1") || 1;
```
